$comment: Who is on the hook for each of the 12 GROUPS in context-map.json — the join .github/CODEOWNERS
does not make.
Sixteen until 2026-09-02, when the four TWINNED groups the 2026-07-30 scan produced were merged
in context-map.json. Four of the rows below used to exist only to say that their group was 'the
scan's second X group' with the same owner, the same rank and the same exposure as its twin —
which is this file recording, in writing, that the taxonomy had stopped deciding anything. The
reasons those rows carried are folded into the survivors rather than deleted.
CODEOWNERS is drawn per FILE and deliberately narrow: it names ~15 law files where a change needs
the maintainer's eyes, and says in its own first line that everything else is open season. That is
the right shape for a review-routing rule and it answers a question nobody has: 'who owns this
line?'. The question this repository actually has is the other one — ~97% of commits are written by
an agent, agents create files inside contexts, and the system is described per GROUP. So a whole
group can drift, gain files, gain cross-group imports and gain unmapped source without anything
being able to say that nobody has read it. `npm run owners:groups` is that sentence.
WHAT A ROW DOES AND DOES NOT DO. It does NOT request a review — GitHub reads .github/CODEOWNERS and
nothing else, and turning every group into a CODEOWNERS path would make one maintainer the required
reviewer of the whole tree, which is how a routing rule stops being read. A row records who ANSWERS
for the group when the weekly triage pass reaches it, and `triageRank` is the order that pass takes
them in: the groups where a wrong change is a bill or a breach are read before the ones where it is
a layout regression. That ordering is the artefact — before this file, the triage order was whatever
the reviewer happened to scroll past.
$howToChange: A group added by a context scan needs a row here in the same diff, or `npm run owners:groups:check`
(blocking, via test-unit/group-owners.test.mjs inside test:unit → check:ci → .husky/pre-push) fails
with the group's name. A group a scan REMOVES takes its row with it, for the same reason a stale
CODEOWNERS path is worse than none: a declaration that has stopped describing the tree still reads
`owner` must be a handle .github/CODEOWNERS already uses. An owner nobody can be routed to is a
name, not an owner — and if a group genuinely needs a second person, they arrive in CODEOWNERS
first, where GitHub can act on them.
$cannotSee: whether the owner actually READ anything — this is a declaration of who answers, not evidence of a review;
whether a group's contexts still describe the tree — that is `npm run agents:surface` (mapped paths that moved) and the 159-file unmapped ratchet;
whether a change CROSSED a group boundary — that is `npm run context:decay:check`, which blocks on a new undeclared crossing;
GitHub's own review routing, which reads .github/CODEOWNERS and never this file.

groups.why: Cron auth, metering, the durable spend ceiling and the store drivers live here. A wrong change is a bill or an unauthenticated endpoint, and three of the five mutation-drill seams are in this group.

The LLM chokepoint and every one of its callers — a change here is a prompt that ships, and the golden, budget and model pins are all downstream of it. Absorbed the scan's second AI group on 2026-09-02: every registered llm-tool sat in one of the two and which one was an artefact of the scan rather than a decision.

The Sklik and Google write rails — SKLIK_WRITES_ENABLED is armed from this group's code and AGENTS.md § Red says an agent may never widen it — plus the tenant-key builder the whole store seam is made of (ADR-0002), where a wrong key is a cross-project read that nothing 401s. Absorbed Campaign Management on 2026-09-02: those two halves of one seam were split across two indistinguishable names.
Holds personal data and the conversion-upload path to Google Ads — one of the outbound edges AGENTS.md § Red reserves for the operator.

Drafts that leave the machine under the operator's name. The review gate in `schranka` is what stands between a generated post and a published one. Absorbed the scan's two-context Social Media group on 2026-09-02 — same outbound exposure, indistinguishable name.
Project creation, deletion cascade and the Offering spine. A missed cascade leaves another tenant's rows addressable after a delete.
The catalog feed and its public token. Small, and one of the few groups with an unauthenticated read surface.
Session and per-project tenancy resolution for /app. Correctness here is the difference between a project switcher and an IDOR.

Reads and aggregates rather than writes: a wrong number is a wrong decision, not a wrong charge — and it is where a spend figure is most likely to be quietly wrong. Absorbed Performance & Analytics on 2026-09-02; the two had the same posture and the same rank, and differed only in which noun came first.
Imported rank data and the map surface. Self-contained; a regression is visible in the product before it is expensive.
The public site. A regression is a bad first impression and is caught by the E2E smoke job, which is a required check.
Shared chrome, tokens and the design system. Imports INTO it are always legal (context:decay treats shared/infrastructure that way), so it is the group most likely to accumulate other groups' code.
